aliases: SG Arrival Card with Electronic Health Declaration

scam_info.sample: Submission of the SGAC is free and should only be done via ICA’s official channels ( SGAC e-Service or MyICA Mobile app ). ... You may refer to the Annex below for some of these entities/websites to avoid. Annex S/N Web Address 1. application[.]singaporevisa[.]com
scam_info.notes: The only official SG government page in this partition with a multi-item domain list. 63 entries, defanged with [.], some with paths, and one has a stray space ("singapore-arrivaldoc [.]com"). Dates: header "Last updated 30 Oct 2026"; footer "IMMIGRATION & CHECKPOINTS AUTHORITY Last Updated: 15 September 2026". The original issue date is not on the page; in Mar 2022 ICA told ST it was aware of 12 such fee-charging sites (https://www.ntu.edu.sg/business/news-events/news/story-detail/websites-charge-travellers-as-much-as-100-dollars-for-help-in-sg-arrival-card-submission). Mix of paid third-party services (e.g. ivisa[.]com) and look-alikes. ICA calls them "entities/websites to avoid", not all phishing. Older mirror URLs seen in search: /public-education/public-advisory-on-websites-offering-services-relating-to-the-submission-of-sg-arrival-card. Change detection: diff the annex. Copy saved at registry/_work/gov_security_digital/artifacts/ica_sgac_annex.txt. scam_info.sample: there is a fake SG Arrival Card (SGAC) website named “Online Singapore Arrival Card” (www.singapore-arrival-card.com/) which ... requests for a payment of US$30/- for submission of the card.
scam_info.notes: Issued 17 Dec 2020. The same domain is annex item 40 on the SGAC advisory.

notes: Official submission is free, only via the SGAC e-Service at eservices.ica.gov.sg (/sgarrivalcard, which redirects to /arrivalcard; 2026-11-26 HTTP 200) or the MyICA app. SPF brand tag "SG Arrival Card (SGAC)" (1 advisory). Highest-value concrete list in this partition: a 63-domain annex. Its access is HTML with no feed, so diff the page.
